en: Air is a mixture of gases that has measurable mass and takes up physical space.
Puddles evaporate into water vapor at room temperature, not just when water reaches its boiling point.
Melting an ice cube changes it from solid to liquid, but the total mass stays exactly the same.
Dissolving sugar in water breaks it into invisible particles, but the total mass of the sugar remains unchanged.
Rusting is a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen and water to form a completely new substance.
Honey flows much slower than water because the liquid honey has a much higher viscosity.
Boiling water stays at exactly 100 degrees Celsius until all the liquid turns into water vapor.
The helium gas filling a party balloon has mass and is pulled downward by Earth's gravity.
Burning wood produces ash, water vapor, and carbon dioxide gas, meaning the original matter is not destroyed.
Objects cool down because thermal energy moves out of them into their cooler surroundings, not because cold enters.
You can separate dissolved salt from water by boiling the mixture to evaporate the liquid and leave solid salt.
True steam is invisible water vapor, while the white cloud above a kettle is actually tiny liquid water droplets.
